text: I was on that stage from the moment the second act went up until the curtain. Two hundred people watched me. And I never set foot in Julian's dressing room last night. Why would I?

assertions.claim: I was on stage from the start of Act 2 until the curtain.
I never went into Julian's dressing room last night.
assertions.note: She did argue with him in the interval, but he walked back on stage alive at 21:05, and she never left it.

text: I sat in the Green Room the whole of the second act, going over my lines in case. I didn't go anywhere. Ask anyone.

assertions.claim: I didn't leave the building during the second act.
assertions.note: He slipped out to a payphone to read for another part, and was on the line for sixteen minutes.

text: I called every cue of that show from the prompt corner. I never left it until I went to fetch him for the curtain call. That's my job.

assertions.claim: I never left the prompt corner during the second act.
assertions.note: She climbed to the fly gallery for three minutes to free a snagged line, in full view of the flymen.

text: I watched every minute of it from Box B, as I have every opening night for eighteen years. I never went backstage; I never go backstage during a show. And Julian was renewing with me. We were closer than ever.

assertions.claim: I never left Box B during the second act.
I never went backstage last night.
Julian was renewing with me. I'd heard nothing about him leaving.
I never went near his dressing room.

text: I was in Wardrobe mending the whole second act. I didn't go near Mr Crane's room. I didn't see anything.

assertions.claim: I was in Wardrobe the whole second act.
assertions.note: She took him a tray of tea at 22:00, found the door locked, and ran. She was afraid to say so.
